plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers. Many cultivars bloom in the cool season, brightening gardens when little else is in flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring (peak in midwinter in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and eastern China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant from which all true tea is made.

plants.name: Hamamelis mollis
plants.description: A deciduous shrub that produces spidery, ribbon-like, fragrant flowers on bare branches in the depths of winter. The petals curl up in freezing weather to protect themselves and unfurl when it warms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midwinter to late winter (December to February)
plants.location: Native to central and eastern China; grown in temperate gardens in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Witch hazel flowers can survive freezing temperatures because their petals roll up tightly in the cold and open again when it warms.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A spreading tree with fern-like leaves and a canopy covered in large, brilliant flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere summer it blooms spectacularly, shading streets and parks in warm regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer (December to February); in the tropics, spring to summer
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in Australia, southern Africa, South America, and the tropics
plants.funFact: This tree is endangered in its native Madagascar even though it is among the most widely planted ornamental trees in the world.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low, evergreen perennial with leathery, dark green leaves and nodding, cup-shaped flowers that open in the coldest months, often pushing up through snow. Its blooms fade to pink as they age.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to the mountain woodlands of central and southern Europe; cultivated in cool temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Despite its name, it is not a rose at all but a member of the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are toxic.
